diffs.diff: header pin 10 (SRCLR): part says power, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: TI SN74HC595 datasheet Table 5-1 lists 'SRCLR 10 I SRCLR Input' (a logic input, so the reading's 'io' is the electrical type), but this model's role field is wiring intent: src/core/autowire.ts wires role 'power' pins to the supply rail. Function Table 8-1: 'SRCLR L -> Shift register is cleared'; shifting requires SRCLR = H. Note (1) under Recommended Operating Conditions: 'All unused inputs of the device must be held at VCC or GND to ensure proper device operation.' The example/driver does not drive SRCLR (srclr=None), so tying it to VCC (role power) is the datasheet-correct wiring; as 'io' it would get a GPIO that is never driven and float. Pin number 10 and name match the datasheet.

diffs.diff: header pin 13 (OE): part says gnd, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: TI SN74HC595 datasheet Table 5-1 lists 'OE 13 I Output Enable' (a logic input), but this model's role field is wiring intent: src/core/autowire.ts wires role 'gnd' pins to board GND. Function Table 8-1: 'OE H -> Outputs QA-QH are disabled', 'OE L -> Outputs QA-QH are enabled'. Note (1): 'All unused inputs of the device must be held at VCC or GND'. The example/driver does not drive OE (oe=None), so tying OE to GND (role gnd) keeps the outputs enabled and the input from floating; as 'io' it would get an undriven GPIO. Pin number 13 and name match the datasheet.
